notes: All divide-before-multiply, incorrect-exp, and too-many-digits findings were in lib/openzeppelin-contracts (out of scope). Filtered.
Semgrep INFO severity findings (gas-only) discarded per policy.
Slither shadowing-local on src/mocks/MockERC20.sol discarded (mock, out of scope).
abi.encodePacked finding is context-only: used to build revert string, not as a hash input. Retained as potential-low.

findings.description: External call to ammAdapter.swap() at line 364 precedes state updates: clientBalances[token][balanceHolder] and totalDeposited[token] are written at lines 371-372 AFTER the external swap. A malicious or compromised AMM adapter could re-enter withdraw flows before principal accounting is decremented.

External call to ammAdapter.swap() at line 426 precedes state writes: clientBalances[token][client] = 0 and totalDeposited[token] -= clientStoredBalance are executed at lines 429-430 AFTER the swap returns. A re-entrant call between the swap and the accounting zeroing would see stale (non-zero) balances.

External call to ammAdapter.swap() at line 318 precedes state writes to clientBalances[token][recipient] and totalDeposited[token] at lines 322-323. A re-entrant deposit via a malicious AMM adapter would see stale balance accounting.

Dangerous strict equality: `totalShares == 0 || totalDeposited[token] == 0`. These values can be manipulated to be non-zero but epsilon small (e.g. dust donation to the vault), bypassing the early-return guard and producing incorrect proportional share calculations (division by very small numbers).

Local variable `lastToken` is declared but never initialized before its first use in the loop body at line 76-78. It defaults to address(0). If path[0] is address(0) (i.e. an empty path), the loop never sets lastToken, and the require at line 80 compares tokenOut against address(0), which passes if tokenOut was inadvertently zero — a mis-configuration guard bypass.

Local variable `totalSetAside` at line 546 is uninitialized (defaults to 0 as uint256 in memory). Slither flags this as a medium; here it is benign by Solidity semantics but indicates a style risk. The real concern is the return value mismatch: the function totals `buf` amounts against `underlyingReceived`, but if `totalSetAside` accumulated incorrectly, underflows in the final subtraction would revert silently. Retained for reviewer attention.

EnumerableSet.add(client) and EnumerableSet.remove(client) return bool (true if set changed, false if already present/absent), but the return values are silently ignored at lines 187 and 189. If the owner calls setClient with an already-authorized address, the call succeeds silently and the ClientAuthorizationSet event still fires, creating misleading audit logs with no state change.

IERC20(_underlyingToken).approve(_erc4626Vault, type(uint256).max) uses the bare ERC20 approve() rather than SafeERC20, and its return value is unchecked. Non-standard tokens that return false on approve (e.g. USDT on mainnet in failure modes) would silently leave the contract without an allowance, causing downstream vault.deposit() calls to revert with an unhelpful allowance error.

`nonReentrant` appears after `onlyOwner` in the modifier list (order: onlyOwner, nonReentrant, whenNotPaused). If any modifier that runs before nonReentrant makes an external call, the reentrancy guard would not yet be active. Current onlyOwner is a local check so this is low risk, but the ordering is non-standard.

`nonReentrant` is not the first modifier on deposit (L229), withdraw (L248), withdrawAsOwner (L265), and totalWithdrawal (L279). The modifiers that precede it (onlyAuthorizedClient / onlyOwner) do not make external calls today, but the ordering creates fragility if modifiers are updated.

AYieldStrategy.setPauser() assigns _pauser = newPauser at line 268 without checking newPauser != address(0). Setting _pauser to address(0) disables the pause mechanism permanently unless the owner calls setPauser again. Corroborated by Aderyn's state-no-address-check.

Constructor parameter `_owner` in AYieldStrategy (L171), ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy (L101), and ERC4626YieldStrategy (L86) shadows the inherited Ownable._owner state variable. This pattern is a common source of copy-paste confusion if the constructor body is modified, as a developer may accidentally read the parameter instead of the state variable.

A require() statement inside the loop at line 511 means a single client whose surplus check fails reverts the entire skimSurplus() call, including all previously-processed clients. If one client's invariant is violated (e.g. corrupted buffer config), the entire surplus collection operation is bricked until the bad client is removed.

vault.convertToShares(surplus) is called inside a loop at line 521, making an external call per client. If the client list is large or if the vault's convertToShares has side effects, this creates a gas DoS vector and multiple external call opportunities.

abi.encodePacked() is used at line 340 to concatenate a string literal with _uint256ToString(executableAt) to build a revert message. This is NOT passed to keccak256, so there is no actual hash collision risk here. Aderyn flags it by pattern. Retained for completeness; real severity is informational.

The Swapped event is emitted at line 140 after the external call to router.exchange() at line 138. If the router triggers a callback, the event emitted would reflect post-callback state rather than the state at the time of the swap initiation. This is a weak reentrancy signal; Curve routers are not callback-based, but the ordering is non-standard.
